ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, within circle $O$, $AB$ is a diameter, and point $C$ is a point on the circle. The minor arc $AC$ is folded along the chord $AC$ to intersect $AB$ at point $D$, and $CD$ is connected. If point $D$ does not coincide with the center $O$ and $\angle BAC=24^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle DCA$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect BC,\\
$\because$ AB is the diameter of $ \odot O$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ACB=90^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle B=180^\circ-\angle BAC-\angle B=180^\circ-90^\circ-24^\circ=66^\circ$\\
According to the reflection property, $\angle B$ is the inscribed angle corresponding to arc $\overset{\frown}{AC}$, $\angle ADC$ is the inscribed angle corresponding to arc $\overset{\frown}{ABC}$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle B+\angle ADC=180^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ADC=114^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DCA=180^\circ-\angle ADC-\angle BAC=180^\circ-114^\circ-24^\circ=\boxed{42^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is circle O, A is on the lower-left side of the circle, B is on the upper-right side, and C is on the lower-right side; segment AB passes through the center O and is a diameter. AC is an approximately horizontal chord, D is located on AB and does not coincide with O, and CD is also drawn in the figure. The diagram also shows the trace after minor arc AC is folded along chord AC. Then reason: According to the method, connect BC, and let D' be the preimage of point D when the folded arc is unfolded along AC back to the original circle. Because AB is a diameter of circle O, by the fact that the inscribed angle subtended by a diameter is a right angle, we get ∠ACB = 90°. It is also known that ∠BAC = 24°, so in triangle ABC, ∠ABC = 180° - 90° - 24° = 66°. The folding is a reflection about line AC; A and C do not move, and angles remain unchanged, therefore ∠ADC = ∠AD'C. After unfolding, B and D' are on the circle and are located on opposite sides of chord AC; the inscribed angles they subtend to the same chord AC are supplementary, so ∠ABC + ∠AD'C = 180°, hence ∠AD'C = 180° - 66° = 114°. Thus ∠ADC = 114°. Because D is on AB, ray AD is collinear with AB, and ∠CAD = ∠CAB = 24°. In triangle ACD, ∠DCA = 180° - ∠ADC - ∠CAD = 180° - 114° - 24° = 42°.
